Operator
Good day, and welcome to the CNX Resources Q4 2025 Q&A Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. Should you need assistance, please signal a conference specialist by pressing the star key followed by zero. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you may press star then one on a touch-tone phone. To withdraw your question, please press star then two. Please note that this event is being recorded. I would now like to turn the conference over to Tyler Lewis, Senior Vice President of Finance and Treasurer. Please go ahead.
Tyler Lewis
VP of Investor Relations, CNX Resources Corporation
Thank you, and good morning, everybody. Welcome to CNX's Q4 Q&A Conference Call. Today, we will be answering questions related to our Q4 results. This morning, we posted to our Investor Relations website an updated slide presentation and detailed Q4 earnings release data, such as quarterly E&P data, financial statements, and non-GAAP reconciliations, which can be found in a document titled "Q4 2024: Earnings Results and Supplemental Information of CNX Resources." Also, we posted to our Investor Relations website our prepared remarks for the quarter, which we hope everyone had a chance to read before the call, as the call today will be used for Q&A. With me today for Q&A are Alan Shepard, our President and Chief Executive Officer; Everett Good, our Chief Financial Officer; and Navneet Behl, our Chief Operating Officer.
Please note that the company's remarks made during this call, including answers to questions, include forward-looking statements which are subject to various risks and uncertainties. These statements are not guarantees of future performance, and our actual results may differ materially as a result of many factors. A discussion of risks and uncertainties related to these factors in CNX's business is contained in its filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission and in the release issued today. Before we get into Q&A, I'm going to turn it over to Alan for a couple of comments related to the recent cold weather events. Alan?
Alan Shepard
President and CEO, CNX Resources Corporation
Thanks, Tyler, and good morning, everyone. We normally don't provide opening remarks on these calls, but I'd be remiss today if I didn't take a moment to acknowledge the hard work and incredible efforts of not just our CNX team, but of all the men and women of the natural gas industry who are working to keep the heat and lights on across America during this extraordinary cold weather event we are experiencing. Speaking on behalf of myself, everyone in the room with me, and all of our fellow citizens who are staying warm today, thank you for everything you've done, everything you will continue to do in the days, weeks, and years ahead. With that being said, Operator, can you please now open the line for questions?
Operator
We will now begin the question-and-answer session. To ask a question, you may press star then one on your touch-tone phone. If you're using a speakerphone, please pick up your handset before pressing the keys. If at any time your question has been addressed and you would like to withdraw your question, please press star then two. At this time, we will pause momentarily to assemble our roster. The first question today comes from Jacob Roberts with TPH. Please go ahead.
Jacob Phillip Roberts
Equity Research Analyst, TPH & Co. Inc
Good morning.
Alan Shepard
President and CEO, CNX Resources Corporation
Good morning, Jacob.
Jacob Phillip Roberts
Equity Research Analyst, TPH & Co. Inc
We wanted to ask about the commentary on the front-half-weighted capital and TIL program and how we should be thinking about that translating to a flat production profile across the year. Just wondering if you can provide any more granularity on how you're thinking about the TIL schedule quarter to quarter?
Everett Good
CFO, CNX Resources Corporation
Yeah, thanks, Jacob. This is Everett. You can generally think about the first half CapEx being about 60% of the year's total. And then from a production basis, it's pretty flat throughout the year. But the weighting of that capital to the first half gives us some flexibility in the second half of the year to potentially accelerate frac activity if conditions warrant.
Jacob Phillip Roberts
Equity Research Analyst, TPH & Co. Inc
Okay, great. That's helpful. And turning to the RNG business line, we're curious to how you view the outlook on the AEC pricing, and is there a pathway to getting that back to the $65 or $75 million annual run rate? And in terms of the 45Z outlook, is it fair to assume that the $20 million are going to gross up $30 million? Is that also firmly tied to the methane stream in terms of the volume being relatively steady going forward?
Alan Shepard
President and CEO, CNX Resources Corporation
Yeah, so thanks for the questions there. Let's start with the PA Tier 1 REC market. So that market's been pretty stable since call it spring of last year. With the Trump administration coming in, it softened a little bit. I think longer-term outlook for that market, the prices you're seeing now are basically what you need to underwrite sort of new solar and wind activity in the PJM markets. So for value per megawatt hour to increase there, you're going to need to see some of the step-ups in the required percent of contribution to the grid from renewables. So that's sort of the long-term bull case as those standards tighten, you just see pricing move up. But in the near term, it's sort of settled into the marginal cost of bringing on new renewable supply.
On 45Z, yeah, I think the way to think about that is current production levels we're able to generate on a run rate basis about $30 million a year with the initial proposed guidance. And we'll see what the final guidance looks like when it comes out and if there's any adjustments to that.
Jacob Phillip Roberts
Equity Research Analyst, TPH & Co. Inc
Great. I appreciate the time.
Operator
The next question comes from Leo Mariani with Roth. Please go ahead.
Leo Paul Mariani
Equity Research Analyst, ROTH Capital Partners
Hi. I was hoping you could talk about the Utica program here in 2026. I'm only seeing kind of three turn-in-lines, probably a little bit lower than I expected. It seems like the company's been very excited about the Utica and made some good progress. So it just seemed like maybe it was a little smaller program this year. So just trying to reconcile that, but maybe some of this is just timing where maybe some of the 26 wells are coming on next year.
Alan Shepard
President and CEO, CNX Resources Corporation
Yeah, I think it's the latter, Leo. I appreciate the question. I mean, it's really nothing to indicate the underlying kind of belief in the Utica or anything like that. It's just we have a lot of TILs from last year coming online. We have some Southwest PA inventory that we want to harvest that's really economic. And then we're going to continue in the last half of the year back at it, reps at the wellhead on the Utica. So I don't know if Nav has got anything to add, but nothing to read into on sort of the TIL timing there.
Tyler Lewis
VP of Investor Relations, CNX Resources Corporation
Yeah, yeah, Leo, I can add. We are really confident of our deep Utica program right now. And as Alan mentioned, this is just a timing issue, nothing else. In fact, we'll be TIL-ing about five Utica laterals this year. So it is a function of timing on when we complete it. Okay. That's very helpful for sure. And then, Alan, you kind of went off the call talking about weather here. Just wanted to get a sense, are you guys expecting some disruption to the operations or the volumes here in Q1? Obviously, it sounds like your team's doing a great job, but just wanted to get a sense if you think there's some impact here.
Alan Shepard
President and CEO, CNX Resources Corporation
No, we're not. So our team's been preparing for the last weeks heading into this event. They've done a tremendous job keeping the field running. The numbers that we put out today include any expected disruptions. So nothing on that front.
Leo Paul Mariani
Equity Research Analyst, ROTH Capital Partners
Okay. That's helpful for sure. And then just lastly on your New Tech business, wanted to get a sense if there's any update in terms of how some of the other businesses are progressing, like AutoSep on the service side. And I know you guys have also discussed kind of some CNG, LNG ambitions over time.
Alan Shepard
President and CEO, CNX Resources Corporation
Yeah. On the AutoSep, I think, as we mentioned before, we fully internalized, adopted that technology. We use it on our flowbacks, provided tremendous cost savings, environmental, and safety benefits. We are the sort of non-op on that. We've outsourced that to an OFS company who's continuing to roll that out across the Appalachia here. Everything we're seeing is it's starting to be adopted, and we think 2026 might be an uptick year for that, but nothing contributing yet materially to the financial bottom line. When it does, we'll provide guidance on that. As far as the other businesses, the tech still exists for those businesses, but just nothing material to update on those right now.
Leo Paul Mariani
Equity Research Analyst, ROTH Capital Partners
Okay, thanks.
Operator
The next question comes from Michael Scialla with Stephens. Please go ahead.
Michael Scialla
Equity Research Analyst, Stephens Inc
Hey, good morning. You guys said in your prepared remarks you expect to be responsive to any material changes in gas prices this year. Everett, you mentioned you'd consider adding a frac crew in the second half of 2026. Wanted to just see, is that built into the CapEx guidance range, that $20 million variance for this year, or any more detail you could provide there would suggest what CapEx could do for the full year?
Alan Shepard
President and CEO, CNX Resources Corporation
Yeah, Michael, yeah, any uptick in activity is not included in our base ranges. What we're seeing right now in terms of pricing, after you get beyond the February contract, where it falls off pretty significantly in terms of the strips. So we're not seeing the price activity yet, though it would kind of incentivize us to add frac activity in the second half of 2026. Yeah, just to add on, we're not going to chase sort of spot activity. When we talk about adding, it would be some sort of long-term call associated with new infrastructure, new power plants, something like that that would really get the 2027, 2028, 2029 strip moving. We're not going to try to jump around to catch a month of pricing.
Michael Scialla
Equity Research Analyst, Stephens Inc
Got it. Okay. And then just wanted to see if you could add any color on the 3 deep Utica wells you turn in line for the quarter. I realize it's early days, but anything you can say there in terms of cost or production?
Alan Shepard
President and CEO, CNX Resources Corporation
I think everything's generally aligned, Nav. Anything to add?
Tyler Lewis
VP of Investor Relations, CNX Resources Corporation
Yeah. Our team has been really working on the drilling cost, and like we had guided, our average Utica cost is about $1,700 per foot. So that's on the cost. And second, on the performance, these wells are in line with our expected performance. And we are pretty confident. And now we are into the spacing evaluation. So we have two spacing tests going on now. One is 1,300-foot spacing, and then second is 1,500-foot spacing. And as we get more results from these tests, we'll be getting that information out.
Michael Scialla
Equity Research Analyst, Stephens Inc
Great. Look forward to that. Thank you, guys.
Operator
The next question comes from Kale Akamine with Bank of America. Please go ahead.
Kale Akamine
Equity Research Analyst, Bank of America Securities, Inc
Hey, good morning, guys. For my first question, I want to ask about coal mine methane volumes. Kind of a modest downtick year-over-year, maybe 0.5 B off 17.5 from last year. Can you kind of help us understand the activity set behind the volumes, how that may compare to last year, and how many years of visibility you have looking forward?
Alan Shepard
President and CEO, CNX Resources Corporation
Yeah, the way to think about it, those volumes are really the primary driver is the underlying mining activity at that particular mine. Our expectation is that we're sort of in that range moving forward, assuming that mine continues to operate. That life of mine is 20+ years. It's a metallurgical mine in Virginia, if you're familiar with it. So really, any sort of wiggle you see in volumes is just a sort of function of the pace of their longwall and what needs degassed.
Kale Akamine
Equity Research Analyst, Bank of America Securities, Inc
Got it. Thank you, Alan. For my second question, can you just remind us on the hedging strategy? What do you guys expect to be done by 2027?
Everett Good
CFO, CNX Resources Corporation
Yeah, yeah, yeah, Tyle can take that. So for 2027, I mean, as we approach that year, we look to be approximately 80% hedged. 2027 is a really good year for us. Right now, we have kind of a weighted average NYMEX price of about $4. So we target that level around there based on what we can get in the basis markets as well. So at $4 kind of swaps, business performs really, really well at that level.
Tyler Lewis
VP of Investor Relations, CNX Resources Corporation
Yeah. We're 60% hedged already on.
Everett Good
CFO, CNX Resources Corporation
Yeah, we're a little over 60% hedged on that.
Tyler Lewis
VP of Investor Relations, CNX Resources Corporation
Yeah. So we'll dive into the rest of that book throughout the year. Given we're already 60% hedged, we can be a little more opportunistic on putting those on. But as Everett mentioned, we'll be at our 80% sort of number heading into that year.
Kale Akamine
Equity Research Analyst, Bank of America Securities, Inc
Got it. Thank you, guys.
Operator
The next question comes from Jeff Bellman with Daniel Energy Partners. Please go ahead.
Jeff Bellman
Managing Director, Daniel Energy Partners
Hi, good morning, everybody. I had two questions. First one, I appreciate the comments around not chasing a front-month gas price or a near price, but maybe just to expand on it, can you frame maybe a little bit more of kind of what you want to see? You mentioned a 2027 strip, 2028 strip. Is this something where you want to get through the winter, kind of see where storage levels end in terms of kind of timing on any kind of increase in activity? Just maybe a little bit more on kind of how you're thinking about level setting from maintenance to maybe something higher. Thanks.
Alan Shepard
President and CEO, CNX Resources Corporation
Yeah. So maybe break it into two parts. I think you think long-term, right? We've been in maintenance of production, give or take, for the last six years. And that's really a function of just the constraints up here in Appalachia, the unwillingness for regulators to allow additional pipelines to get gas to where it should go. And then some of the projects you are seeing for potential in-basin demand, they're sort of longer lead projects with the new power and AI demand. We're hopeful on those, but they're still a few years out. So there's no reason to build those volumes just yet.
In terms of jumping up or down 5% any given year, to make that decision as part of your planning cycle, you'd want to be able to have pretty good visibility that the prices aren't going to slip away from you by the time you bring the volumes on. So you'd want to hedge off that if you were going to increase production. And then you're just always trying to manage your till count and your DUC count to give you a little bit of flexibility. But that's all just sort of short-term tactics as opposed to sort of the longer-term strategy, which we'd like to see, which is actual increase on the demand side.
Jeff Bellman
Managing Director, Daniel Energy Partners
Great. Yeah. So a follow-up question on that. Can you just speak more broadly on incremental takeaway? I get it on the greenfield difficulties, but I'm hearing more and more there's smaller projects, brownfield expansions, moving gas west out of Pennsylvania into Ohio, kind of some of the bigger data center growth. Just any thoughts on how everybody's doing in terms of kind of pushing a little bit more gas west and south?
Alan Shepard
President and CEO, CNX Resources Corporation
Yeah. A lot of the low-hanging fruit on those western bound projects was taken up last decade. I mean, there are some proposed on the table that get you back sort of to the Midwest area, right, the Leb kind of area. But those haven't been greenlit yet. I mean, the cost of some of those projects is just a little bit challenging just yet. I think everyone's sort of waiting to see sort of what the final outlook is here on AI demand, right? You need kind of those guys to make their decisions, and then we'll be right behind them with the fuel supply to support all that. But yeah, there's some cats and dogs out there, but nothing material to kind of move anybody off maintenance production, in my view.
Jeff Bellman
Managing Director, Daniel Energy Partners
Gotcha. Thank you very much.
Operator
Again, if you have a question, please press star then one. The next question comes from Betty Jiang with Barclays. Please go ahead.
Betty Jiang
Equity Research Associate, Barclays Capital Inc
Good morning. Thank you for taking my question. I have a question on the 2026 activity of going to do the 3 wells in Marcellus in CPA and 3 wells in Utica. I've been surprised just with the Marcellus activity. What's your expectation for the Marcellus productivity in that region?
Alan Shepard
President and CEO, CNX Resources Corporation
Yeah. So the way to think about that, that's kind of our stacked pay development, right? So we're going first with the Utica, and then you're just thinking about putting incremental laterals above that on the Marcellus. I think you're in the sort of just shy of 20 range, right, with the high ones on those wells.
Betty Jiang
Equity Research Associate, Barclays Capital Inc
Got it. And back to your core Southwest PA Marcellus, where you're focusing most of your activity, could you just remind us what is your latest inventory runway in that area if you maintain at the 2026 level?
Alan Shepard
President and CEO, CNX Resources Corporation
Yeah. So I think we'll put out the updated acreage counts at the end of Q1, but generally, we're in the 40,000 to 50,000 acres sort of remaining. So it'll get you towards the end of the decade.
Betty Jiang
Equity Research Associate, Barclays Capital Inc
Okay. Got it. That's it. Thank you.
Operator
This concludes our question-and-answer session. I would like to turn the conference back over to Tyler Lewis for any closing remarks.
Tyler Lewis
VP of Investor Relations, CNX Resources Corporation
Great. Thank you for joining us, everyone, this morning. Please feel free to reach out if anyone has any additional questions. Otherwise, we'll look forward to speaking with everyone again next quarter. Thank you.
Alan Shepard
President and CEO, CNX Resources Corporation
Thanks, everybody.
Everett Good
CFO, CNX Resources Corporation
Thank you.
Operator
Thank you. The conference has now concluded. Thank you for attending today's presentation. You may now disconnect.

This morning, we posted to our Investor Relations website an updated slide presentation and detailed Q2 earnings release data such as quarterly E&P data, financial statements, and non-GAAP reconciliations, which can be found in a document titled "Q2 2025 Earnings Results and Supplemental Information of CNX Resources." With that, thank you for joining us this morning, operator, can you please open the call for Q&A at this time?
Operator
Certainly. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. As a reminder, to ask a question, you may press Star, then one on your telephone keypad. If you are using a speakerphone, please pick up your handset before pressing the keys. If at any time your question has been addressed and you would like to withdraw your question, please press Star, then two. At this time, we will pause momentarily to assemble our roster. Your first question comes from Zach Parham with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.
Zach Parham
Executive Director, JPMorgan
Hey, thanks for taking my questions. I wanted to ask on the Section 45Z tax credit. Could you just give us a little detail on the timing and ability to claim those credits? As the rules are laid out today, would those credits just run through 2029?
Alan Shepard
President and CFO, CNX
Yeah. Hi, Zach. Good question. The way the program's set up currently, right, as the initial rule guidance, as you point out, there needs to be final rulemaking. As long as everything comes in line with the initial guidance, the first year eligibility to claim credits would be in 2025. If you saw in our materials, we were talking about 2026, would be the first potential opportunity to get some of that $30 million a year run rate. Yeah, the program got extended under the OBBV through 2029. It'd be the first time that it'd be up for re-extension.
Zach Parham
Executive Director, JPMorgan
Thanks. Also just wanted to ask on activity levels at the E&P business.
Alan Shepard
President and CFO, CNX
Mm-hmm.
Zach Parham
Executive Director, JPMorgan
Any plans to grow volumes here? I know at one point y'all talked about having optionality to add some activity back in the H2 of the year. If not can you talk about what a maintenance program might look like in 2026? Would that be flattish CapEx year-over-year? Just trying to get a sense of what activity levels may look like.
Alan Shepard
President and CFO, CNX
Yeah. maybe on the first one we were positioned with some optionality had we seen sort of the end-of-year storage levels stay low. I mean, at this point it's pretty clear that we're going to creep towards four TCF in storage. under that scenario, we're just going to maintain the initial set of activity that we'd planned for the beginning of the year. no changes expected at the current time. When we think about sort of capital efficiency levels, I think the way to do that is to sort of tie back to what we guided to a few years back or a few quarters back.
The two numbers that stand out are sort of the 580 million of production or 580 Bcfe of production over the $500 million CapEx. That ratio is about $0.85 per million in terms of capital efficiency. I think moving forward if you set aside the actual production we'll target, which we always talk about as being a function of optimizing free cash flow per share, that's the right ratio to think about the business' capital efficiency moving forward, that mid-eighties range. It'll wiggle plus or minus a little bit any given quarter, just with the lumpiness with the one rig program, but that's the right way to think about it moving forward.
Zach Parham
Executive Director, JPMorgan
Thanks, Alan. Appreciate the color.
Alan Shepard
President and CFO, CNX
Yep.
Operator
Your next question comes from Leo Mariani with Roth. Please go ahead.
Leo Mariani
Managing Director and Senior Research Analyst, ROTH
Yeah. Good morning here. wanted to see if you could get a little bit more color on drilling and completion activity levels in the H2. I know y'all had said that CapEx was pretty front half weighted, in 2025. Just looking at your turn-in-line schedule, the vast majority of turn-in-lines, it looks like they happen here, in Q1. If you could maybe speak to whether or not there's a bit of a lull, in activity here in the H2, and maybe that activity picks up, a little bit in the winter. Could you also relate that to CapEx trends?
I mean, it looks like CapEx is down a little bit in Q2 versus Q1, and maybe just help a little bit with the trajectory on CapEx in the H2.
Alan Shepard
President and CFO, CNX
Sure. Sort of similar to what we talked about last time, Leo, Basically, the bulk of the TILs were weighted toward the front half of the year. Our next batch of TILs would be towards the latter part of Q4. What you'll see on the production front is sequential declines. It'll be lower in Q3 and then lower in Q4 until that next batch of TILs comes on. CapEx will track that, right? CapEx will be lighter in Q3 and then pick back up in Q4 when we get back to it on the activity front.
Leo Mariani
Managing Director and Senior Research Analyst, ROTH
Okay. It sounds like there's a bit of a hiatus in activity, then it picks up late this year to get you all ready for the winter in 2026. Is that the way to think about it?
Alan Shepard
President and CFO, CNX
Yeah, that's the right way to think about it. You know, we're going to continue to run the one rig program on the drilling side, and then completion activities will hit a bit of a lull. Those will pick back up in the fall as we get ready for the TILs that I talked about in the December timeframe.
Leo Mariani
Managing Director and Senior Research Analyst, ROTH
Okay, that's helpful. Then just on the Utica, obviously y'all seem excited about that. Sounds like the costs are already below your target here on the wells. That's nice to see. You know, at this point, given you've beaten the target, do you think there's more room to go on the cost side or maybe that can come down? Apart from the cost, could you speak to the actual well results, production performance? How are the results trending versus your expectations? Maybe just overall, how do you see this competing with the Marcellus?
Navneet Behl
COO, CNX
Leo, good morning. This is Navneet. Just wanted to outline on the Utica. We've done a really team's done a really great job on optimizing our drilling and completion operation over the last couple of years. We're really pleased with the performance so far, but we're not satisfied yet. We are aggressively trying to improve the performance over the next few quarters. Stay tuned on where we can get down our, increase our operational efficiency and reduce our costs. That's one.
Second, on the performance, all our Utica wells, our performance are within our expectations and our latest TILs that we got in Q2 are slightly above our expectation. We are really excited about the deep Utica play, and we look forward to continuing to get more wells in there.
Alan Shepard
President and CFO, CNX
Leo, maybe I'll address the last part of your question on how we think about the Utica and the Marcellus mix. We've been very intentional in giving Nav and the operating team a nice runway here to really demonstrate their prowess in being able to drive these costs down. Moving ahead, obviously we're going to continue to develop our core Southwest PA field over the next few years. We also, as Nav pointed out, we want to keep getting him reps at the Utica wellhead there, so he can continue to work on cost efficiencies.
Leo Mariani
Managing Director and Senior Research Analyst, ROTH
Okay. Appreciate all the detail. Thank you.
Alan Shepard
President and CFO, CNX
Yep. Thank you.
Operator
Your next question comes from Noel Dunn with Bank of America. Please go ahead.
Noel Dunn
Managing Director, Bank of America
Good morning. I was hoping to ask on Section 45Z again.
Alan Shepard
President and CFO, CNX
Yeah.
Noel Dunn
Managing Director, Bank of America
When do you think you'd be able to reach that $30 million a year run rate? When you do realize the full $30 million of additional free cash flow from Section 45Z, should we think that all of your RMG gas would be sort of shifted to qualify for this Section 45Z opportunity? Will some of it still be used to qualify for the PA AEC Tier 1 credit?
Alan Shepard
President and CFO, CNX
The way to think about timing is, like I said, so 2025 is the first year of eligibility for the program, but the cash associated with that wouldn't occur until you file your tax return for 2025 and 2026, right? That's when you would create the tax credit that would be fungible, and you could convert that to cash in the market. In terms of volumes that qualify, I mean, bigger picture, our initial read on the guidance is that it's stackable, so you're able to take advantage of both programs in terms of Section 45Z and the Pennsylvania Tier 1 REC. The volumes don't qualify one for one, so some volumes might qualify under Tier 1 RECs, and some volumes might qualify under Section 45Z.
It's a, it's a blend of which ones do and which ones don't. You know, at this time, it's all still subject to that final rule. You know, we're optimistic as long as things follow the initial guidance, but there's still a bit of waiting, wait and see on that.
Noel Dunn
Managing Director, Bank of America
That's helpful color. For my second question, could you maybe talk about what credit price is underwriting the revised environmental attribute free cash flow guide of $65 million?
Alan Shepard
President and CFO, CNX
Yeah. It's sort of where the market's at now. We treat it very similar to how we report the open prices for the rest of the year. You just look at the PA Tier 1 strip, that's in the mid-twenties right now for the megawatt-hour.
Noel Dunn
Managing Director, Bank of America
Okay. Thank you.
Alan Shepard
President and CFO, CNX
Yep.
Operator
Your next question comes from Jake Roberts with TPH. Please go ahead.
Jake Roberts
Director, TPH
Good morning.
Alan Shepard
President and CFO, CNX
Good morning.
Jake Roberts
Director, TPH
Maybe a bit of a follow-on to that last question. Should we be thinking about the $30 million as a function of the, of the RMG input or the result of some sort of downstream output?
Alan Shepard
President and CFO, CNX
Well, the tax credit is for the incentivizing the collection of waste gas off the backside of coal mines and creating a saleable product into the pipeline, if that makes sense. That's why it's thought about more as remediating a, or abating a, an emission source.
Jake Roberts
Director, TPH
Okay, that's helpful. Then I just wanted to give you guys the opportunity to talk a little bit about the AI and Energy Summit. I know you mentioned it in the release. Specifically, we're wondering how much the RMG product is factoring into those conversations with any counterparties, maybe in particular the tech guys. Ultimately, do you think there is a pathway for RMG to get better economics on some of the potential deals there?
there relative to the current pathways you've laid out?
Alan Shepard
President and CFO, CNX
Yeah, great question. No, we're super excited. You know, our mantra around here is Appalachia first. All of this AI stuff is going to be great for the region, great for the industry. In particular, you nailed our lane that we're super focused on right now, which is offering the RMG product to the market as a true sustainable energy solution, to get the folks that are using nat gas down to a zero carbon sort of profile on these new data centers. Obviously, we're having discussions with folks. You know, we have third-party marketers having discussions with folks, and we're excited to see that develop and not just on the existing volumes, but enough incentive from the voluntary markets to go out and gather some additional volumes, hopefully.
Nick DeIuliis
CEO, CNX
Jake, this is Nick, just to sort of follow on with Alan. The way we look holistically at the AI opportunity and remediated mine gas RMG, it's another industry pathway, whatever you'd want to call it, to get the value of it recognized and utilized. We started with manufacturing and arm's length transactions that recognized it for manufacturing downstream products. We've got it recognized, of course, in the power grid under the Pennsylvania PUC. We then were able to get it recognized in the hydrogen economy with Section 45V, now transportation of alternative fuels with Section 45V. This would be another critical pathway that I think makes a whole bunch of sense and has a certain level of inevitability to it. The timing and the magnitude of it's still a TBD.
Jake Roberts
Director, TPH
Great. Appreciate the time, guys.
Alan Shepard
President and CFO, CNX
Yeah. No problem.
Operator
Your next question comes from Michael Scialla with Stephens. Please go ahead.
Michael Scialla
Managing Director, Stephens
Hi, good morning, everybody. Just to follow on the AI topic there, obviously a lot of news recently on gas providing power for data centers in the region. Just wanted to get your updated thoughts on in basin demand. Does that have any impact on your long-term view of natural gas prices in your hedging strategy?
Alan Shepard
President and CFO, CNX
I don't think it has any impact on our hedging strategy in the short term. You know, our hedging strategy is a function of how we manage the balance sheet and how we manage our overall capital allocation program. I think long term, it's absolutely going to be bullish. You know, anything that creates in basin demand, given our interstate pipe restrictions that we've experienced over the last decade, is going to help everyone in basin. It's we're more of in wait and see mode, you know. From our position, it's we have the depth of inventory. You know, we have the ability to deliver gas. It's just now wait and see which projects come online and how we can benefit from that.
Nick DeIuliis
CEO, CNX
Yeah. Michael, I think to the prior experiences that we've had in similar types of opportunities for the industry and for the region, when you're looking at potentially new demand being created, that journey to where we end up actually versus what we're hearing and what people are projecting today, it's obviously going to be very different. There's going to be all kinds of factors and changes and twists and turns. As to which plants get built and when they're online and what the timing of all that is, there's just a lot of things to be figured out between today and then the future. I think you saw that too since the summit with what's going on with volatility on pricing.
That's why we basically love the opportunity and the developments it would mean for demand for natural gas and what it could mean for the region in terms of sort of a reindustrialization, a revitalization of a lot of these communities. In terms of taking positions today and speculation of what that's specifically going to mean when it comes to things like hedge book and capital allocation, our playbook, our philosophy, our approach remains exactly the same.
Michael Scialla
Managing Director, Stephens
Yep. Makes sense. Wanna get your thoughts on the Q2 production surprise a little bit. Wanted to see if you could pinpoint where that came from. Was it new wells outperforming expectations, base decline, anything else?
Navneet Behl
COO, CNX
Hi. Our production outperformance was basically like four things coming together for us. The first one is our new TILs performance. The Apex Marcellus wells and our Utica wells, they've done really well. The second part is our operational execution, which has given us opportunity to move some of this forward. The third part is our production efficiency gains on our, on our base production. We are doing really well there. The last part is like our uptime on base production. All four combined led to this result.
Michael Scialla
Managing Director, Stephens
Sounds good. Thank you very much, guys.
Operator
Your next question comes from Betty Jiang with Barclays. Please go ahead.
Betty Jiang
Senior Equity Research Analyst, Barclays
Good morning. Thank you for taking my question. I want to go back and ask about the deep Utica results again. In your view, how much do you think costs will have to come down for the deep Utica to compete with Marcellus returns? Broadly speaking, from what we can tell, the Utica wells are fairly concentrated right now. Would love to get your thought about the consistency of Utica performance on your acreage?
Alan Shepard
President and CFO, CNX
Yeah. I would say on the first question, where we're at right now on sort of the cost structure, we think that makes those wells competitive with best in basin opportunities, even on the Southwest PA sort of Marcellus stuff. The longer term we're going to step out from where we're at now, but our expectation is that there's a pretty long runway across our field up there to make these results repeatable.
Betty Jiang
Senior Equity Research Analyst, Barclays
Okay, thanks. A follow-up on the new tech. Just as related to the gas power for AI, when you think about your value recognition for the gas, is it fair to think about it from a voluntary carbon credit perspective where you're selling the attributes to tech companies looking to reduce their carbon footprint? Is it through compliance market or other channels?
Alan Shepard
President and CFO, CNX
Yeah. On the RMG front, we're going to sell to whichever market recognizes the highest value, right? I mean, currently that is the latter, the one that you pointed out. It's the renewable energy credit markets for the existing RPS programs. There is a a finite amount of this resource that's available. We think the environmental attributes should result in some voluntary pricing that rivals the regulatory pathways in the long term.
Nick DeIuliis
CEO, CNX
Betty, you also bring up another good point with the question, which is the focus currently, right, has really shifted with the opportunity of AI in places like Appalachia to nat gas demand and the construction of the data centers and power plants to power them, et cetera. There's also another issue that's been there from the get-go that will remain. It just maybe has perhaps fallen a bit below the radar, which is the sustainability solution or the sustainability path to making all this growth occur. The ultimate sort of clients and drivers of that, the tech industry hasn't sort of backed up with regard to sustainability or carbon goals one step since they originally set them. This new growth option for them is going to make that even more of a heightened challenge.
I think RMG playing a role in how this ultimately plays out has never been in more demand. To your point, I think the tech industry will play a key role in that.
Betty Jiang
Senior Equity Research Analyst, Barclays
I'm sorry if I could just follow up on that answer. Thank you.
Alan Shepard
President and CFO, CNX
Sure.
Betty Jiang
Senior Equity Research Analyst, Barclays
The voluntary carbon market perspective, would that be incremental to PA REC market or Section 45E?
Alan Shepard
President and CFO, CNX
Yeah. At some point you can only sell into one market. Traditionally the voluntaries, depending on which pathway you're using, they might not be stackable. It's all very facts and circumstances dependent, so hesitate to give a general answer, but the way to think about it is you can generally get maybe one to two stacking, but you're not going to get beyond that.
Nick DeIuliis
CEO, CNX
Yeah. Think of it as another pathway that would compete with your other alternatives.
Alan Shepard
President and CFO, CNX
Yeah.
Nick DeIuliis
CEO, CNX
Currently not stackable.
Betty Jiang
Senior Equity Research Analyst, Barclays
Got it. Thanks.
Operator
Again, if you have a question, please press star then one. Your next question comes from David Deckelbaum with TD Cowen. Please go ahead.
David Deckelbaum
Managing Director and Senior Analyst, TD Cowen
Thanks, Nick and Alan and team, for taking my questions today.
Alan Shepard
President and CFO, CNX
Yeah.
David Deckelbaum
Managing Director and Senior Analyst, TD Cowen
I just wanted to follow up on just the Utica mix. You talked about just giving more at bats next year. As we just think about the general activity level that you guys have laid out, should we think about the Utica taking more share of the program over the next couple of years, or is there still some more headway to make on the cost side before it becomes a larger contribution?
Alan Shepard
President and CFO, CNX
No, I would go back to what I said on one of the with your earlier questions. I think at this point in the cost structure, these wells are in the mix in terms of IRR competitiveness, so you're going to see them in the program moving forward. What we're really trying to do is balance the harvesting of the Southwest PA sort of field that's fully developed with the any potential step out in the new CPA area. You know, we look at every project on a full cycle IRR basis, and that's how we determine the mix. Like I said, we've been very intentional recently in just giving Nav lots of at bats to demonstrate for repeatability.
Moving forward, I think we're comfortable that we can be super focused on just the best projects at the right time.
David Deckelbaum
Managing Director and Senior Analyst, TD Cowen
Appreciate that. You know, just to follow up on conversations just around marketing and obviously in-basin demand. As you said today, we go into winter, you guys talked about before hitting tank tops or so as we get into fall sort of setting up for 2026. You know, there's been a lot of contracts that seem like they're in the early days of being signed right now. From where you sit, do you think it's sort of best to see this market get appreciably tight over the next few years and see in-basin demand increase before signing long-term agreements? Or is that something that you think is going to be in your relative near future?
Alan Shepard
President and CFO, CNX
Yeah. I think the first signal you want to see is a, an actual data center connected to some of the nat gas projects. I think once you see the first sort of data center sign up for electricity offtake here in Appalachia, that'll give folks a real sense of how the value is going to get distributed across the chain. Until you see that you're a little bit hesitant to lock in your respective ownership of that economics. As Nick pointed out, there's still a lot of innings here. We're still very early, but there's some definite value in to wait and see how this plays out before locking up anything long term.
David Deckelbaum
Managing Director and Senior Analyst, TD Cowen
Appreciate it. Best of luck, guys.

This concludes our question and answer session. I would like to turn the conference back over to Tyler Lewis for any closing remarks.
Tyler Lewis
VP of Investor Relations, CNX
Thank you again for joining us this morning. Please feel free to reach out if anyone has any additional questions. Otherwise, we'll look forward to speaking with everyone again next quarter. Thank you.

content.text:
Tyler Lewis
VP of Investor Relations, CNX Resources
Thanks, and good morning to everybody. Welcome to CNX's Q1 Q&A Conference Call. Today, we will be answering questions related to our Q1 results. This morning, we posted to our investor relations website an updated slide presentation and detailed Q1 earnings release data such as quarterly E&P data, financial statements, and non-GAAP reconciliations, which can be found in a document titled 1Q 2025 Earnings Results and Supplemental Information of CNX Resources.
Also, we posted to our investor relations website our prepared remarks for the quarter, which we hope everyone had a chance to read before the call, as the call today will be used exclusively for Q&A. With me today for Q&A are Nick DeIuliis, our President and CEO, Alan Shepard, our Chief Financial Officer, and Navneet Behl, our Chief Operating Officer.
Please note that the company's remarks made during this call, including answers to questions, include forward-looking statements which are subject to various risks and uncertainties. These statements are not guarantees of future performance, and our actual results may differ materially as a result of many factors. A discussion of the risks and uncertainties related to those factors in CNX's business is contained in its filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission and in the release issued today. With that, thank you for joining us this morning. Operator, can you please open the call up for Q&A at this time?
Operator
Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. Again, to ask a question you may press star then one on your touchtone phone. If you're using a speakerphone, please pick up your handset before pressing stars. If at any time your question has been addressed and you would like to withdraw your question, please press star then two. Our first question will come from Zach Parham with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.
Zach Parham
Executive Director and Equity Research Analyst, JPMorgan
Hey, thanks for taking my question. I guess first, just wanted to ask on activity levels. You all had a significant amount of turn-in-lines in Q1 with 19. Can you talk about, you know, the rest of the turn-in-lines during the year? When do those come in line? Maybe comment on what the production trajectory should look like through the back half of the year and maybe into 2026.
Alan Shepard
CFO, CNX Resources
Yeah. Hey, this is Alan. A lot of those wells came online in the latter part of Q1. As we had mentioned on the last call, the bulk of some of our completions activity was gonna be scheduled in the first half of the year. You'll see a few more wells in Q2, and probably a lull in Q3, and then some additional wells coming in in Q4.
Zach Parham
Executive Director and Equity Research Analyst, JPMorgan
Thanks. And then just wanted to follow up. On the Q4 call, you talked about having the flexibility to add some activity to the program in the second half of the year. Given the volatility we've seen in gas prices, you know, how are you thinking about flexing that activity? And maybe talk about, you know, the timeline on when you would have to make a decision on whether or not to add some activity.
Alan Shepard
CFO, CNX Resources
Yeah. Right now there's no planned changes to the activity set. We'll kind of watch it through this part of the shoulder season here and we see where end of summer storage is targeting and go off that as our cue.
Zach Parham
Executive Director and Equity Research Analyst, JPMorgan
Thanks.
Operator
Our next question will come from Leo P. Mariani with Roth Capital Partners. Please go ahead.
Leo Mariani
Managing Director and Senior Research Analyst, ROTH Capital Partners
Hey, just a couple quick questions here on some of the numbers here. Looks like you guys actually paid some cash taxes in Q1. A little bit surprising. Generally thought you guys weren't gonna be paying much on the cash tax side. Just curious if that was kind of a one-off. Then just on the buyback, kind of very robust number here in Q1, you know, $125 million, you know, pretty big number. You know, I guess, is it fair to think that kind of around this $30 level, you guys think it's a pretty compelling, you know, investment here on the buyback?
Alan Shepard
CFO, CNX Resources
Yeah. On the cash taxes front, we're still a de minimis cash taxpayer. You know, if you're seeing noise trying to reconcile deferred tax to things, that's basically from the hedge book. We don't become a material tax cash payer until about $3 billion in cumulative free cash flow, which is the current projections call sometime 2027, 2028, as we've talked about previously. There is a little bit of state tax starting to hit, but again, that's all very de minimis. In terms of your latter question, yeah, I think, you know, we're always, we see value in kind of the repurchases when we do them as part of our process.
Leo Mariani
Managing Director and Senior Research Analyst, ROTH Capital Partners
Okay. Appreciate that. I just wanted to ask if you guys have got any kind of further intel in terms of how the Trump administration might be looking at, you know, changes in Section 45Q here.
Alan Shepard
CFO, CNX Resources
No, we don't have anything outside of what's in the public domain.
Leo Mariani
Managing Director and Senior Research Analyst, ROTH Capital Partners
Okay. Thank you.
Operator
Our next question will come from David Deckelbaum with TD Cowen. Please go ahead.
David Deckelbaum
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, TD Cowen
Thanks. Hey, good morning, everyone. Maybe just following up on Zach's question earlier. Could you maybe just give us a sense then of what volume trajectory looks like? Imagine just given a heavy first half, you're declining into the second half and probably into 2026. So what's the production level that you guys would like to hold flat into 2026? Is it 1.4 Bs a day on the gas side? And if that's the case, what's the CapEx level needed to hold that flat into 2026?
Alan Shepard
CFO, CNX Resources
Yeah. I think if you take kind of the detail comments I made earlier, you can kind of infer from that, you know, if you wanna do quarterly production. Again, we don't get too tied up in looking at quarterly production, and even annual production levels. You know, we have kind of a range we've been in the last few years, and I would expect going forward would be in that sort of range plus, you know, the volumes associated with Apex. Again, you know, we're solving for free cash flow per share as opposed to any particular production level target.
David Deckelbaum
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, TD Cowen
Understood. Thanks for that. Then I guess just as a follow-up, some M&A in your backyard recently, maybe just any kind of updated thoughts on the transaction that just changed hands recently in Westmoreland and generally your views on future opportunities in the area. Thank you, guys.
Alan Shepard
CFO, CNX Resources
Yeah. No, we think it kind of reinforces what we've been saying for the last decade, which is that particular area of the basin is some of the best rock that's gonna be moving forward. You know, from our perspective, we have significant acreage position up there. We're excited to have a new neighbor that's kind of validated our thesis on the area.
David Deckelbaum
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, TD Cowen
Gotcha. Thanks, guys.
Operator
Our next question will come from Noah B. Hungness with Bank of America. Please go ahead.
Noah Hungness
VP and Equity Research Analyst, Bank of America
Morning, guys. For my first question here, I was hoping to ask you on slide six. It looks like your NYMEX and NGL pricing has kinda declined as you guys kinda mark to market with strip moving down, and then also the natural gas differentials seem to have widened a bit. Your free cash flow guidance for the year is unchanged. Could you kinda walk us through some of the potential improvements in the base business that's kinda driving that free cash flow resiliency?
Alan Shepard
CFO, CNX Resources
Yeah. Just a reminder, we're 85% hedged. When you see the open volumes pricing change, you're really talking about just, call it three-quarters of exposed pricing at this point on 15% of the volume. There's not a huge amount of wiggle room associated with open pricing left for the full year. Then, you know, the free cash flow guidance we give, it is a point number, but it's really sort of a range around a number. I wouldn't get overly specific in trying to reanalyze it. We'll be in that range. We're reaffirming that range.
Noah Hungness
VP and Equity Research Analyst, Bank of America
Got it. We've seen some power gen and data center announcements in that, kinda in that southwest central PA area. I was just kinda hoping to get your guys' latest view on how you see in-basin demand developing and if you think we'll continue to see announcements over the next 6 to 12 months.
Alan Shepard
CFO, CNX Resources
Yeah. In my opinion, I think you're gonna see a lot of announcements, and we'll see how many of those translate into actual construction. Overall, bullish for all the operators in the basin, very similar to any sort of utility coming in, as I'm sure everyone will be able to benefit from the increased in-basin demand and shrinking of differentials associated with that. We'll see which ones actually develop, but generally, a great backwind to have for everyone.
Noah Hungness
VP and Equity Research Analyst, Bank of America
Sounds good, guys. Thanks.
Operator
Again, if you have a question, please press star then one. Our next question will come from Jacob Roberts with TPH. Please go ahead.
Jacob Roberts
Equity Research Analyst, TPH
Morning.
Alan Shepard
CFO, CNX Resources
Morning.
Jacob Roberts
Equity Research Analyst, TPH
I was hoping to hear some thoughts about the Apex turn-in-lines that happened during the quarter, just how those are performing relative to the base business and the outlook there.
Alan Shepard
CFO, CNX Resources
Yeah. Go ahead.
Navneet Behl
COO, CNX Resources
Hi. This is Navneet Behl. Yeah, the eight wells that we brought online from Apex Energy, they are pretty productive, better than we expected. We are pretty optimistic about the long-term production on these wells.
Jacob Roberts
Equity Research Analyst, TPH
Great. Thanks. My second question, I think you guys have spoken to there not necessarily being a correlation between attribute sales in the Buchanan Power Facility. I'm just hoping to clarify if that facility showing up on the PJM deactivation list will have any impact on that segment or if there are any other of those types of deactivations we might need to be thinking about.
Alan Shepard
CFO, CNX Resources
That won't have any impact on our EA sales. We use multiple facilities across PJM to create those credits.
Jacob Roberts
Equity Research Analyst, TPH
Thanks. Appreciate the time.
Operator
This concludes our question and answer session. I would like to turn the conference back over to Tyler Lewis for any closing remarks.
Tyler Lewis
VP of Investor Relations, CNX Resources

We will now begin the question and answer session. Again, to ask a question, you may press star, then one on your telephone keypad. If you are using a speakerphone, please pick up your handset before pressing the keys. To withdraw your question, please press star then two. Our first question today comes from Gabe Daoud with TD Cowen. Please go ahead.
Gabe Daoud
Managing Director, TD Cowen
Hey, thanks. Morning, everyone. Was hoping to start first on New Technologies and specifically 45V. Would you be able to walk us through your interpretation of guidance and whether the existing partnership with KeyState Energy will move forward? I guess I had thought that even with flaring as the counterfactual, the carbon intensity of CMM would still put you in a position to recognize maximum credit value. Would love, I guess, a bit more understanding on that.
Ravi Srivastava
President of New Technologies Group, CNX Resources
Yeah. Thanks for the question. This is Ravi. I think you had quite a few layers in that question, so let me try and address them one after the other. Like first of all, the rule provided some important federal recognition for capture of coal mine methane as a low carbon intensity feedstock for hydrogen production, and we're pretty excited about that. Kind of validates CMM's potential to decarbonize a range of, you know, hard-to-abate sectors. With this inclusion, like you know we have successfully validated the premium nature of our coal mine methane, you know, previously in manufacturing, then in power, and now we have validation within the hydrogen production sector.
While we're excited about the recognition of CMM in 45V and the way the first productive, you know, rules came out, that was pretty good. There were quite a few restrictions that were introduced within the rules, which we believe are inconsistent with the scientific assessment of CMM that was done by the national labs and what the intent of the IRA was. We're looking for what the new administration will have an opportunity to kind of improve the rules to ensure there is clarity to make necessary investment decisions in the future to kind of scale this hydrogen economy.
Like our participation and moving some of these projects forward is gonna be contingent on clarity on these rules going forward.
Gabe Daoud
Managing Director, TD Cowen
Okay. Got it. You need more clarity before moving forward on anything. Okay. Thanks for that. Then I guess as a follow-up, I'll switch gears to the E&P side. Could you maybe just talk a little bit about the H2 of 2025 with the H1 being or capital being heavily weighted to the H1? Obviously, would expect some declines in the H2 into 2026. Any additional commentary on maybe timing of re-accelerating activity or what you would need to see to spend more capital in 2025? Any additional clarity there would be helpful. Thanks, everyone.
Alan Shepard
CFO, CNX Resources
Yeah. This is Alan. The way we think about it, we position the activity set. Basically, the whole production flat coming through 2024. The activity set is primarily weighted upfront in Q1. We need to wait and see kinda where the industry production levels are coming out of winter. We need winter to finalize our storage, where projected storage is gonna be, and then we'll make an assessment. We do wanna create that flexibility. If prices stay high or go higher, you could see us accelerate some activity and bring up some more volumes, but it's too early to tell at this point.
Gabe Daoud
Managing Director, TD Cowen
Got it. Thanks, guys.
Operator
The next question is from Zach Parham with J.P. Morgan. Please go ahead.
Zach Parham
Executive Director of Equity Research, J.P. Morgan
Thanks for taking my question. Wanted to follow up on the 2025 budget. I mean, it seems very efficient and seems to be benefiting from some drops on the Apex asset. Could you just give us some color on what the run rate spending would be if you were gonna hold this level of production flat going forward?
Ravi Srivastava
President of New Technologies Group, CNX Resources
Yeah. I think we talked about this at the beginning of last year. The goal, kind of a run rate is sub 500, and there's two things driving that rate. We're starting to see the efficiencies from the Utica CPA development combined with our kind of low decline PDP base. We're comfortable on the legacy assets that you can hold that below 500 for the upcoming years. With respect to Apex, you know, we had the wells that are gonna come online here. Basically, those wells were completed post-close. All we need to do is kind of flow those back and turn them in.
Ultimately, what we do with the acquisition, we'll see, and that goes back to the earlier comment about production levels on that asset are gonna be set by market pricing later in the year as part of our capital allocation process.
Zach Parham
Executive Director of Equity Research, J.P. Morgan
Got it. Thanks for that color. Wanted to follow up on Gabe's question. You know, you spoke about 45V, but could you talk about other potential pathways to generate credits from the CMM business in the future? Just really trying to think about, you know, what could be next for this environmental attributes business.
Ravi Srivastava
President of New Technologies Group, CNX Resources
Yeah. You know, like we've been talking about this where, you know, coal mine methane offers a clear environmental and economic advantage, you know, as an energy source. We have successfully validated that it's premium pricing in manufacturing with a deal like Newlight, you know, in the power generation sector with, you know, qualification of the ATS type program. Now, through 45V for hydrogen production. We're gonna continue to target these different sectors, whether it's in power generation, manufacturing, you know, data centers, all, you know, and the validation that we get from recognition of these programs kind of open up a lot of other monetization opportunities.
We'll keep driving those efforts, and we'll share more information as we have more updates to share on that front.
Zach Parham
Executive Director of Equity Research, J.P. Morgan
Thanks a lot.
Operator
The next question is from Leo Mariani with Roth. Please go ahead.
Leo Mariani
Managing Director and Senior Research Analyst, ROTH Capital Partners
Hi. Just wanted to dive in a little bit more to some of the NewTech numbers here. It looks like Q4 of 2024 saw very robust free cash flow at $30 million. As we're kind of looking ahead, you know, into 2025, seemingly you guys are guiding to say that NewTech free cash flow will be down a little bit this year. Maybe you could just provide a little color around that given the strength that we saw, you know, in Q4. Then just additionally, you know, have you seen any real contribution yet from the oilfield service business or the CNG, LNG business in 2024 to that free cash flow? And do you expect those businesses to be additive here in 2025?
Ravi Srivastava
President of New Technologies Group, CNX Resources
Yeah. This is Ravi again. The Q4 numbers are kind of primarily, if you remember in Q3, we had a lower volume, we had a lower cash flow number because some of the volumes got pushed into Q4. The Q4 numbers are kind of benefiting from monetization of more, you know, environmental attributes in the Q4 volume itself, in Q4 itself. The overall volume is consistent, and we were able to kind of bring some volume that would have been monetized in January, kind of got into December, which allowed the Q4 number to be high.
On a run rate basis, I think the volumes that we'll be able to monetize into that ATS program is in that 17 to 18 BCF. The value recognition is kind of still staying in that, say, $30 to 35 per megawatt hour range. I think that's gonna be the primary driver for the free cash flow in that segment, which kind of comes out to that $75 million-ish per year range. There may be like some ebbs and flows because of when some of those volumes get monetized, largely that's what the driver is. The AutoSep and CNG business, they're still in early commercialization phase.
I mean, AutoSep is fully deployed on CNX's footprint, and we're seeing the cost benefits, the safety benefits, operational efficiencies, and emission reduction, you know, objectives that we wanted to achieve with that. We're seeing that on that front. Expansion beyond CNX's footprint, we expect to see in 2025. As some of that materializes, we'll share more information.
Leo Mariani
Managing Director and Senior Research Analyst, ROTH Capital Partners
Okay. That's helpful. Then obviously I think in your comments, you folks referred to hopefully the new administration here, which has come in, might take a fresh look at the 45V rule interpretation and maybe make some more favorable, you know, changes. Just, you know, overall, obviously you have 45Q legislation, you know, pending, you know, as well. Clearly, we had the red sweep, you know, that happened with the elections here. I mean, it's been, I guess, you know, a short period of time, just a couple of weeks since the Trump administration has taken over.
Do you folks have any read on how the new administration would just kind of be viewing coal mine methane in terms of, you know, the abatement there and how that can kind of translate into potential opportunities for you folks? Has there been any signal at the administration that they're more inclined to maybe be helpful on this front?
Ravi Srivastava
President of New Technologies Group, CNX Resources
I mean, I would say it's too early at this point in time. I mean, coal mine methane has a lot of inherent environmental and, you know, socioeconomic benefits. I think we're gonna continue to advocate and make the case for it. 45Q and other processes like that, they're gonna run their political, you know, due course. We'll stay connected in that with the right folks. You know, in the meantime, we're gonna continue to pursue opportunities in these other markets and sectors for monetization pathways.
Leo Mariani
Managing Director and Senior Research Analyst, ROTH Capital Partners
Okay. No, that's helpful. Just jumping over to some of your comments on production just real quick. Just wanted to kind of make sure I sort of understood them. You know, really the goal here of 2025 production is to kind of keep your base volumes flat. It sounds like, if I heard you right, you'll expect to see some maybe modest declines on the Apex volumes maybe as we get into the H2 of the year. I know you're bringing some , you know, kind of online, which will happen for little to no capital. Maybe that props up production in the near-term, but then you kind of see a modest decline, you know, in the H2.
Just wanted to make sure I sort of, you know, heard that right. It sounded like also if conditions though are more favorable in the gas market and the rest of the winter is decent, then there's a reasonable chance you might have a few more wells late this year with maybe the goal to kind of flatten that out as we head into the end of the year in 2026.
Alan Shepard
CFO, CNX Resources
Yeah, that's right. You know, the guidance we provided kind of speaks to what you're talking about with the optionality to increase volumes or accelerate volumes in the H2 of the year if the pricing and capital allocation methodologies suggest we should do that.
Leo Mariani
Managing Director and Senior Research Analyst, ROTH Capital Partners
Okay. Okay, thank you for the clarification.
Operator
The next question is from Bertrand Donnes with Truist. Please go ahead.
Bertrand Donnes
Financial Analyst, Truist Financial
Hey, morning, guys. On the coal mine methane front, I just wanna make sure I understood your comments correctly. You're only looking for clarity on the overly restrictive rules, but if those are cleared up, the financial incentives are enough. Is that correct? You know, is there any capital levels that would be associated if, you know, the rules were clarified positively that maybe a CapEx you'd have to spend?
Ravi Srivastava
President of New Technologies Group, CNX Resources
Hey, Bert. I think the restrictive nature of the rules and, like, there's some lack of clarity on, you know, the book and claim methods and which, like, facilities qualify. There's a lot there to unpack. I think it's gonna take a little bit of time to figure out, you know, like how all those things kinda shake out. Once we have a better idea of, you know, all those things, I think that'll provide a better understanding of like, you know, what the, how the plan forward could be in terms of capital investments and like, you know, where those capital investments are made.
There's just too much lack of clarity at this point in time, and it's gonna take a little bit of time to figure out how the rules get fixed and then how some of the more clarifications from Treasury and DOE on some of the other applications kinda comes in. Too early at this point in time to comment on that.
Bertrand Donnes
Financial Analyst, Truist Financial
Okay. Just to make sure. There is some level of if the rules were clarified positively, you would have some level of, you know, revenue, but then maybe you could increase that amount by spending some capital. I guess there's room to accelerate, activity through, you know, operations.
Nick DeIuliis
President and CEO, CNX Resources
This is Nick. Just to be clear and back up a step. Where we're at with coal mine methane and the climate benefits tied to it as a fuel stock blend to different industries. We've got manufacturing, where it's established a premium pricing level. We've got the hydrogen economy now with the recently issued 45V guidance, and we've got the power generation sector with programs like the AEPS standards in Pennsylvania. We're continuing to work all those different avenues to optimize that portfolio, and some of that is going to involve things like 45Q and 45V, and some of that will include pursuing opportunities in things like the AI power generation industry to feed it, and recognizing the benefits in market transactions with regard to fugitive methane capture.
With respect to these individual rules and programs, it's part of a bigger puzzle, and it's too early to say. We'll have to wait and see where it lands.
Bertrand Donnes
Financial Analyst, Truist Financial
That's perfect. Thank you. Just the other question would be on the buyback activity. I was just a little bit surprised you didn't step in in, you know, Q1 of 2025. Were there maybe some blackout periods due to Apex or maybe a view on the macro? Or is it maybe a game of we should preserve the capital if we want to accelerate in the H2 instead of using it on buybacks now, or just any thoughts there? Thanks, guys.
Alan Shepard
CFO, CNX Resources
Yeah, I think we talked about before. It doesn't, we don't talk about tactics on these calls. I think we just refer back to them. We do run a continuous capital allocation process, and obviously there is a blackout period, that's part of that consideration.
Bertrand Donnes
Financial Analyst, Truist Financial
Understood. Thanks, guys.
Operator
The next question is from Michael Scialla with Stephens. Please go ahead.
Michael Scialla
Managing Director, Stephens
Thank you. Good morning, everybody. Wanted to ask on the Apex acquisition, you talked about 8,600 net acres there of undeveloped Utica. Just wondering with that, you know, that acquisition being 36,000 acres, was the Utica developed on a large portion of that acreage, or is it limited by geology? Just looking for a little bit more color there.
Alan Shepard
CFO, CNX Resources
Yeah. Our view is that there's developable Utica across that footprint, and there hasn't been any development on that particular asset just yet on the Utica.
Michael Scialla
Managing Director, Stephens
Does that imply that there's upside to that 8600? I guess I'm just looking at how did you come to the 8600 number.
Alan Shepard
CFO, CNX Resources
The $8,600 that we disclosed on the acquisition, you're saying, on the Utica?
Michael Scialla
Managing Director, Stephens
Yeah. In terms of
Those are controlled-
In terms of.
Yeah. Those are controlled rights at acquisition. That's what they had in terms of
Oh, got it.
Alan Shepard
CFO, CNX Resources
Utica under lease.
Michael Scialla
Managing Director, Stephens
Gotcha. They didn't have rights.
Alan Shepard
CFO, CNX Resources
Yeah.
Leo Mariani
Managing Director and Senior Research Analyst, ROTH Capital Partners
Okay, got it. Or 36,000, sorry. Of those eight wells that are gonna be turning in line on that acreage, are all those Marcellus or any of those Utica?
Alan Shepard
CFO, CNX Resources
Those are all Marcellus.
Michael Scialla
Managing Director, Stephens
Okay. Just one more on Utica. Just, are you still thinking kinda three Bcf per 1,000 foot of lateral? Any update on what you're seeing with cost per lateral foot in those wells?
Navneet Behl
COO, CNX Resources
Yeah, Mike, that's correct. The wells that we, you know, gave guidance last quarter, like the BP6 and the Noel, they are holding production like we expect it to. They are in line for three Bcf per 1,000 feet.
Michael Scialla
Managing Director, Stephens
Anything on the cost side that you can say there?
Alan Shepard
CFO, CNX Resources
I'll just say, you know, part of the capital efficiency number that you're seeing in the total CapEx, we're delivering these wells, you know, at the target numbers we're looking to see. I think there's a little bit of room to improve, and we're gonna continue to work on that. We're very pleased with where we're at on the drilling and the capital efficiency side on those wells.
Michael Scialla
Managing Director, Stephens
Great. Appreciate it, guys.
Operator
The next question is from Noah Hungness with Bank of America. Please go ahead.
Noah Hungness
Equity Research Associate, Bank of America
Morning, Nick and team. I guess the first question here is also on the Utica. If you guys could give any latest thoughts on spacing, just for new drill locations.
Navneet Behl
COO, CNX Resources
Yes, I can do that. This is Nav. On the spacing, so far, with the BP6 wells, they are at 1,300-foot spacing. That's in line. We have a few more spacing tests coming up at 1,500 feet. We will be able to, like, talk about that, you know, later this year.
Noah Hungness
Equity Research Associate, Bank of America
Appreciate it. My second question is just on cash taxes for 2025, how we can think about that given how volatile strip has been?
Alan Shepard
CFO, CNX Resources
Yeah. We're still a de minimis cash taxpayer until we reach kind of a cumulative $3 billion of free cash flow. We don't see material kind of cash tax payments until we get out to late 2026, early 2027.
Noah Hungness
Equity Research Associate, Bank of America
Great. Thanks.
Operator
The next question is from Jake Roberts with TPH. Please go ahead.
Jake Roberts
Director, TPH & Co
Morning.
Navneet Behl
COO, CNX Resources
Morning.
Jake Roberts
Director, TPH & Co
I wanted to touch on the comment about coal mine methane volumes relative to the referenced anticipated mining plans. Can you give any insight into how much insight you guys might have into those plans and the timeframe of that mine development we should be thinking about? Is that comment on development specific to the Buchanan complex? It seems like you guys may be capturing almost all of the drainage gas there, but it appears there may be other mines at smaller volumes that could present some opportunities. Are there any limitations on capturing those volumes?
Navneet Behl
COO, CNX Resources
Yeah. Our volumes are primarily Buchanan Mine at this point in time. I mean, we have some capture operations in our Northern Appalachian footprint as well. Director, TPH & Co

Yeah, you know, marketing is on a daily basis, right? We're continually optimizing with our FT portfolio, which end markets we hit. Jake Roberts
Director, TPH & Co
Thank you. Appreciate the time.

This concludes our question and answer session. I would like to turn the conference back over to Tyler Lewis for any closing remarks.
Tyler Lewis
